subject: Authentication Refactor & Session Management
verdict_justification: The refactor implements the core session lifecycle correctly, but contains an unhandled race condition in token renewal and lacks audit logging for revocation events.
standard: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet requirements
Session renewal must be race-condition free under concurrent requests
All security-sensitive events must produce audit log records
Type-safe error returns with no raw exception leakage

requirements.evidence: Refresh token rotation exists but lacks mutex locking during DB write
revokeSession() deletes database record without emitting log event

issues.title: Concurrent refresh token rotation window
issues.why_it_matters: Simultaneous API requests with the same refresh token trigger double rotation errors and revoke the session.
issues.impact: Legitimate active users get logged out unexpectedly when opening multiple tabs.
issues.evidence: src/auth/session.ts:142 has a 200ms window between read and invalidate.
issues.proposed_fix: Use atomic database CAS (compare-and-swap) or Redis mutex lock on refresh token consumption.
issues.commentary: Implemented atomic compare-and-swap update query in src/auth/session.ts with 500ms grace window for in-flight requests.

issues.title: Missing revocation audit trail
issues.why_it_matters: Security incident response cannot verify who terminated an active session.
issues.impact: Compliance failure against SOC2 telemetry standards.
issues.evidence: src/auth/session.ts:189 invokes deleteSession directly with no logger call.
issues.proposed_fix: Add auditLog.emit('session.revoked', { userId, sessionId, timestamp }) before DB deletion.

issues.title: Token expiry error message exposes server clock skew
issues.why_it_matters: Error string includes exact epoch timestamp difference.
issues.impact: Minor information disclosure, low exploitation value.
issues.proposed_fix: Return generic `Token expired` error string to client.

dismissed: Memory leak in session cache — cache is bounded LRU with 10k items and TTL eviction, memory remains stable.

verification.source_note: Official Node.js documentation; backed by OpenSSL RAND_bytes

verification.claim: Token rotation prevents replay attacks without grace periods
verification.source_note: RFC 6749 Section 10.4 recommends grace period or atomic lock to handle network race conditions

unknowns.what: Database write latency under peak load
unknowns.what_would_resolve_it: Run k6 load test simulating 500 concurrent renewals
unknowns.materiality: Determines whether CAS lock requires an external Redis coordinator

strengths: Constant-time token comparison prevents timing attacks
Clean separation of token issuance and session persistence concerns
regrets: Did not model concurrent refresh token edge cases during initial architecture review
process_changes: Add concurrency integration tests for any stateful credential exchange protocol
plan_1hr: Implement compare-and-swap update query for refresh token rotation
Add audit log emit on session revocation
plan_unlimited: Extract distributed session coordinator service with formal TLA+ state machine verification
